text:
kevin: heads-up — the gpu-watchdog is cordoning nodes on single Xid37 spikes. we had 5 rapid cordons this morning and it knocked model capacity in us-east-1. can we discuss tightening heuristics (consecutive windows + capacity check) before doing a full drain? cc @maria @sophia

maria: +1. propose a two-stage approach: 1) soft-taint the node on first anomalous signal, 2) require N occurrences within T minutes to escalate to cordon+drain. track both xid errors and ecc_uncorrected. metric names we use: gpu.xid.count, gpu.ecc.uncorrected. cooldown after recover = 30m.

sophia: important: Slurm jobs will requeue and blow up scheduling if we drain during a big batch. we need slurm integration: set node to MAINT (or drain in Slurm) when we go hard, and prefer migrating jobs off GPUs rather than evicting if possible. also avoid draining more than 1 node per AZ in a single policy run.

alex: agree on soft vs hard flow. sketch of K8s flow: soft -> annotate + taint (NoSchedule) so new pods don't land; observe for 3 incidents in 5m -> cordon + drain. sample commands we could use in watchdog:
```
# soft taint
kubectl annotate node $NODE gpu-watchdog/soft=true --overwrite
kubectl taint nodes $NODE gpu-watchdog/soft=true:NoSchedule || true
# promote to hard after checks
kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
We should run drain with --pod-selector for only GPU workloads to avoid cascading non-GPU evictions.

infra-bot: watchdog-runner: triggered on node gpu-node-42 — observed Xid37 x2 within 2m; applied soft taint.

kevin: two operational notes: 1) capacity check: if available free GPUs in the cluster < 12% we should NOT escalate to drain unless node is confirmed hardware-fail (ecc_uncorrected > 0 or nvml reports fatal). 2) check node pool type: if node is preemptible/spot then we might prefer marking for replacement in autoscaler instead of draining heavy-prod pods.

maria: pseudocode for capacity check:
```
free_gpus = metrics.query("sum(node_gpu_free)")
total_gpus = metrics.query("sum(node_gpu_total)")
if free_gpus / total_gpus < 0.12:
  mark_as_soft_only()
else:
  escalate_to_drain()
```
Also recommend a safety cap: don't hard-drain more than 3 nodes in a 30m window cluster-wide.

sophia: alerting tweak: create an alert when soft-taint_count > 20 across cluster and page on pagerduty (severity P2). this helps catch noisy periods before capacity is impacted.

alex: will draft the rollout plan: implement watcher logic in canary (us-west-2 small pool) -> 48h observation -> flip global. add feature flag in infra-config. also add runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-watchdog (draft).

kevin: sounds good. action items: alex drafts PR with script + tests, maria wires capacity check into metrics, sophia adds slurm MAINT integration and alert, i'll schedule a 30m sync if PR is ready for review. :thumbsup:
